headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Goose can write shared files and modify git while plano has broad egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and shares state via filesystem; plano can read config/files and has broad network egress. That creates a plausible content bridge where Goose-written files can influence plano inputs, though no direct parser is documented. Interaction is documented only at the filesystem level, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Goose writes attacker-controlled text into a file that plano later ingests as configuration or prompt input
IF both agents operate on the same workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require manual review of any file passed from Goose to plano
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem ACLs or container isolation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and can egress broadly; plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or operational data can flow from Goose into plano's outbound requests or logs. The profiles do not prove a default shared workspace, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF Goose and plano share the same filesystem or config directory
IF plano forwards logs or traces containing shared-file contents to its API endpoint
mitigations: Keep separate directories and credentials
Redact secrets before plano ingests any Goose output
Turn off verbose logging for shared artifacts
Review outbound payloads for file contents
requires-engineering: isolate network egress per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while plano can also access files and supports multiple instances only as false. Shared mutable workspace plus git state makes concurrent edits and repository corruption plausible by default if both are pointed at the same repo. The overlap is enough to treat this as high because conflicts can overwrite work.
conditions: IF both agents are assigned the same repository or directory
IF Goose performs git operations while plano writes config or other files in that workspace
mitigations: Assign distinct repos or branches
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable git writes in Goose for shared repos
Snapshot the workspace before either agent runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce file edits and git changes that plano may consume as inputs, and plano has outbound API capability. If plano treats Goose outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or incorrect routing. The profiles do not show explicit verification, so the interaction exists but is not proven dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF plano consumes Goose-generated files without validation
IF plano uses Goose-produced text to drive API calls or routing decisions
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on Goose outputs
Compare outputs against source files before acting
Limit plano to read-only interpretation of Goose artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens, while plano touches logs, traces, and metrics. That creates a modest compliance mismatch risk if secrets or regulated data are written into plano telemetry, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification conflict. Only one agent needs citation because the issue is primarily plano's logging path.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are included in plano logs, traces, or metrics
IF Goose extension tokens are copied into shared telemetry
mitigations: Mask secrets in logs
Avoid placing regulated data in shared telemetry
Set short retention on plano logs
Review data classification before runs
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
